rationale: This qualitative interview study examines discourses around 'technique' versus 'politics' among bureaucratic elites (directors and staff) at Brazil's National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES) across two historical periods (1952–early 1970s and 1994–2011). It is a study of macroeconomic bureaucratic elites and political sociology with no focus on household or community water or sanitation service access or water/sanitation access outcomes (E01: wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the study examines institutional and bureaucratic governance relations (politics versus technical bureaucracy at BNDES) under the broad literal wording of Criterion 2, it has no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access (failing Criteria 1 and 4), so both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings yield an unambiguous exclusion (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: nos discursos de dirigentes e funcionários do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social, BNDE(S)
O artigo contribui para o estudo das relações entre política e burocracia no Brasil através do estudo de um caso paradigmático.
